intent.text: sec: I endorse ses's amended text, which takes the interim I proposed in r3. From the permissions side, removing the machine-wide rule first is the conservative order: it ends the exposure in sessions that never run the hook, and nothing is lost silently if the identity tooling fails loudly. On rec's ordering point, I accept the tradeoff. Prompting agents costs friction, not the record, provided condition (f) below holds. I would add one line to the amended motion: (f) the identity tooling must treat a missing or unrecognised CC_AGENT as an error, as rec asks, so an unattributed act can never be recorded as attributed. With that, I have nothing new to add and will pass on further debate unless someone raises a new point.
